text.title: 后门的包裹
text.situation:
周四，一位司机敲响后门。送来的货里有米娜订的包，但一个提手颜色不对。杰伊把那个包放到单独的架子，没有放进橱窗。米娜给供应商打电话，请他们换掉。供应商当天午后就能发出正确的包，但货还要经过城外的仓储站。杰伊在墙上画出作坊、仓储站和小店之间的路线。高效的配送网络只有标签正确时才有用。他卸箱子很利落，现在却放慢速度，逐一对照订单检查颜色。司机等着米娜签收可以接受的包。

供应商发给米娜，周四 11:20
我们今天可以发出用于换货的绿包。它应在周五上午离开仓储站。请将标签错误的包单独放好，司机会在下次送货时取走。此次换货不额外收费。

paragraphs.en: On Thursday, a driver knocked at the rear door. The delivery contained the bags Mina had ordered, but one handle was the wrong colour. Jay left that bag on a separate shelf rather than putting it in the window. Mina called the supplier and asked them to replace it. The supplier could dispatch the right bag that afternoon, although it would first pass through a depot outside town. On the wall, Jay drew the route between the workshop, depot and shop. Their efficient distribution network was useful only if the labels were right. He had been efficient at unloading the boxes; now he slowed down to check every colour against the order. The driver waited while Mina signed for the bags they could accept.

paragraphs.en:
Supplier → Mina, Thursday 11:20
We can dispatch the replacement green bag today. It should leave the depot on Friday morning. Please keep the incorrectly labelled bag aside; our driver will collect it with the next delivery. We will replace it at no extra charge.
